Title: The Nativity
Artist: Sir Edward Coley Burne-Jones (British, 1833-1898)
Date: 1888
Medium: oil on canvas
Classification: paintings
Department: Fine Arts
Accession number: 1997.26.2
Credit line: Heinz Family Fund
Date acquired: 1997-06-05
Location (2017 record): Gallery 5, Scaife Galleries
Acquisition method: Purchase
Provenance: Sir Edward Coley Burne-Jones [1833-1898]; commissioned by Church of St John the Apostle [1861-], Toquay, England, in 1888; (sold at Sotheby's, London, England, November 21, 1989, lot 31); Lord Andrew Lloyd Webber [1948-], London, November 21, 1989 until 1997; purchased by Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburgh, PA, February 1997.

“Miniature Portrait of General James O'Hara” is a drawings and watercolor in the collection of the Carnegie Museum of Art (CMOA) in Pittsburgh, by Henrietta  Agnes  Ridley.
Title: Miniature Portrait of General James O'Hara
Artist: Henrietta  Agnes  Ridley (American, 1847)
Date: 1919
Medium: watercolor
Classification: drawings and watercolors
Department: Fine Arts
Accession number: 39.2.5
Credit line: Gift of Mrs. Alberta McLean
Location (2017 record): Not on View
Acquisition method: Gift
Provenance: H. Agnes Ridley; Mrs. Alberta McLean, until 1939. Gift to Carnegie Museum, Section of Archaeology and Ethnology, but immediately taken to Historical Society of Western Pennsylvania as indefinite loan on February 17, 1939; [transferred to AODA, 1957]; returned to CI for photography for National Portrait Gallery catalogue, 7/3-10/1979; returned to CMNH (Anthropology) February 1981; transferred from CMNH to HSWP, 1994/2000. Family relationships: James O'Hara Mary O'Hara m. William Croghan Mary O'Hara (daughter) m. C.W.H. Schenley H. Agnes Schenley m. Charles Ridley (H. Agnes Ridley is artist) Alberta Ridley m. Mr. McLean (Alberta McLean is donor)

title: The Old King (Carnegie Museum of Art)
text:
“The Old King” is a painting in the collection of the Carnegie Museum of Art (CMOA) in Pittsburgh, by Georges Rouault.
Title: The Old King
Artist: Georges Rouault (French, 1871-1958)
Date: 1916-1936
Medium: oil on canvas
Classification: paintings
Department: Fine Arts
Accession number: 40.1
Credit line: Patrons Art Fund
Date acquired: 1940-05-09
Location (2017 record): Gallery 11, Scaife Galleries
Acquisition method: Purchase
Provenance: Georges Rouault [1871-1958], Paris, France; Ambroise Vollard [1866-1939], Paris, France, until July 1939; estate of Ambroise Vollard, July 1939 until March 1940 [1]; purchased from the estate by Department of Fine Arts, Carnegie Institute, Pittsburgh, PA, March 1940 [2]. Notes: [1]. See curatorial file for copies of correspondence from John O'Connor, Jr., October-December 1939, regarding ownership of the painting (Carnegie Institute archives, Archives of American Art.) [2]. The painting was included in the 1939 International Exhibition of Paintings (1939 Carnegie International.) Director reported the purchase (on March 4, 1940) to Fine Arts Committee on May 9, 1940, "in accordance with action taken at the meeting of December 6, 1939." Guillaume Lerolle, Paris, France served as agent.

Rosenbloom [1898-1973], Pittsburgh, PA (Lugt Suppl. 633b), 1939 until October 11, 1950 [1]; gift to Department of Fine Arts, Carnegie Institute, Pittsburgh, PA, October 1950. Notes: [1]. Mr. Rosenbloom purchased the painting from the 1939 International for $850. It came to the museum on December 15, 1949 and was accessioned the following year, on October 11, 1950. Title: Still Life with Brioche (Nature morte à la brioche)
Artist: Edouard Manet (French, 1832-1883)
Date: 1880
Medium: oil on canvas
Classification: paintings
Department: Fine Arts
Accession number: 84.8
Credit line: William R. Scott, Jr. Fund
Date acquired: 1984-02-02
Location (2017 record): Gallery 6, Scaife Galleries
Acquisition method: Purchase
Provenance: Edouard Manet [1832-1883], until 1880; purchased by Dr. Thomas W. Evans [1823-1897], Paris, France, 1880 until November 14, 1897 [1]; bequest to the Thomas W. Evans Museum and Institute Society, Philadelphia, PA, November 1897 until June 1912; Thomas W. Evans Museum and Dental Institute School of Dentistry University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA, June 1912 until November 15, 1983 [2]; sold at Christie's, New York, NY, November 15, 1983, no. 57 [3]; William Russell Scott, Jr., Pittsburgh, PA and Los Angeles, CA, November 15, 1983 until February 2, 1984; acquired by Museum of Art, Carnegie Institute, Pittsburgh, PA, February 1984 [4]. Notes: [1]. Bought from the artist for 500 francs. See Anne Coffin Hanson's article "A Tale of Two Manets" in "Art in America," December 1979, p. 59. [2].

Provenance: Blanche F. And John T. Galey, Somerset, PA The table was commissioned by Mr. and Mrs. John T. Galey for their house, Galecrest in Somerset, PA. Galecrest was rebuilt after a serious fire in 1958. In early 1959 the Galeys asked Nakashima to design and build a large table for the main room of the house. Nakashima was sent plans of the house and the Galeys described the room and invited Nakashima to visit which he did. In October Nakashima sent back sketches. In his initial sketches the table top was supported by solid ends. The Galeys responded that a more open approach might look "more attractive" given the other furnishings in the room, the proposed position of the table, and the use of the room and the table.
